classification.habit: Evergreen to semi-evergreen small to medium tree
classification.habitat: Forests and foothills of tropical and subtropical regions
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in India and South/Southeast Asia

identification.description: A tree with simple alternate leaves; the fruit is characteristically covered with reddish glandular powder, the source of the crude drug Kampillaka.
identification.whole_plant: Small to medium tree with a rounded crown.
identification.stem: Woody branched stem with grey-brown bark.
identification.leaf: Simple alternate leaves, broadly ovate to lanceolate, often paler beneath.
identification.flower: Small unisexual flowers in axillary inflorescences.
identification.fruit: Small capsules densely covered with reddish-orange glandular hairs/powder.
identification.seed: Small seeds enclosed within the capsule.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Mallotus philippensis fruit glands contain characteristic secondary metabolites; exact profiles vary by extraction and plant material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Kampillaka is a traditional crude drug obtained from the glandular fruit surface. Modern evidence should be interpreted by preparation and indication.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authenticate the reddish glandular material and do not infer dose from crude appearance alone.

exam_points: Drug is reddish glandular powder from fruit surface
viva_questions: What is the useful drug material?
mnemonics: Kampillaka = Kamala powder on the fruit surface.
student.quick_revision: Kampillaka is the reddish glandular material associated with Mallotus philippensis fruit.

teaching_points: Demonstrate crude-drug morphology rather than only whole-plant identification.
discussion_points: Traditional Krimighna use and limits of modern evidence
practical_points: Observe colour, texture and attachment of glandular material.

doctor.quick_reference: Kampillaka — Mallotus philippensis; glandular fruit powder is the listed useful part.
key_precautions: Verify dose and preparation from authoritative references.
